publication_and_concurrency_limits: The existing native publish_new_files reserves outputs exclusively, writes through retained handles, checks parent/reservation identities, and removes still-owned outputs on detected failure. This is not an atomic transaction across all files. Failed invocations/staging/partial diagnostic artifacts must never be treated as successful selected artifacts.

The native publisher does not provide a universal hostile late-hardlink or all-concurrency guarantee. Output identity checks do not prove a directory or inode can never be aliased after a check. No outside-path hardlink attack was performed here.

Native write_validated_ingredient validates schema before writing but is not itself an exclusive transaction or scientific validator. These helpers rely on fresh confined output paths and unchanged declared inputs; final pre/post preservation and exact review receipt binding remain necessary.

Assembly/lineage inputs and some catalog parses use ordinary reads rather than a single atomic filesystem snapshot. Root must keep the declared frozen corpus/packets unchanged and verify their preservation; these controls do not prove resistance to a malicious concurrent input rewrite.

Omission/duplicate tests cover the exact58 flagged-disposition accounting and explicit frozen-case/backlink requirements; they do not establish that any arbitrary supplied provenance plan is scientifically complete. Final approved plan/input hashes remain essential.
